analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of SSDPrefixCache.swift (1–1255) and the complete changed-range patch. The change at HEAD 1790–1800 adds an optional unusedSince cutoff to retirement and forwards it to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove; existing calls retain nil by default. The visible forwarding remains under removalLock and the hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot guards. No concrete regression is established by this change alone.
Against T-041/A-001 and TB-007, examined salt-bound staging lookup and ticket pinning (BASE 511–575), reservation release on adoption/shutdown (430–476, 616–651), donation eligibility and byte caps (841–947), HMAC-only block/sidecar metadata (1057–1071, 1220–1236), sliding freshness updates and bounded write submission (985–1126, 1195–1208). These surrounding behaviors are outside the complete changed ranges; their existing timing-oracle and external-storage limitations are not new findings. No visible changes affect authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing, privileged helpers or installer execution.
Integration must examine SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove and the new cutoff callers: confirm cutoff semantics, fresh-entry/index consistency, and synchronization with index.touch/mtime refresh before deletion. That implementation and caller evidence is absent here, so freshness/TTL and availability effects of the new conditional retirement remain unresolved rather than proven vulnerabilities.
